turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hello there! How's your day treating you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Honestly, a little stressed, but okay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My son has dyslexia and he's started saying he hates books. What can I do?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That must be hard to hear. Audiobooks are a great way to keep him loving stories while reading gets easier.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Isn't that kind of giving up on reading, though?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: No, it's a different road to the same place. Listening builds vocabulary and imagination. Many kids do both, listening and following along in the printed book.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: His teacher mentioned special fonts. Do those actually help?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Some kids find them easier, some don't notice a difference. It's worth a try, along with bigger spacing between lines.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then use that. Short nonfiction books about dinosaurs with big pictures can make reading feel like his thing again.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You're clearly paying attention, and that matters a lot. Keep it fun and low pressure.
